text:
Marta: Quick proposal for a quantized-run protocol (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit) so we can make fair perf + quality comparisons across kernels and batching. High level: separate warmup, force power cap for 'power' runs, canonicalize tokenization, lock kernel selection policy per variant, capture KV-cache stats and NVTX ranges.

Ben: +1. Can you sketch the exact steps? Especially how we should handle KV warmup vs measured inference?

Marta: Sure — suggested flow: 
1) Calibration pass (if needed) — do offline calibration with the same prompt set, store scales.
2) Warmup phase — run many short prefixes to populate KV cache & JIT/kernels. Record only after warmup.
3) Power sweep (optional) — run target power caps for throughput/latency tradeoff.
4) Steady-state measurement — fixed seed, fixed batch profile, measure p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s), peak GPU mem, and quality metric (perplexity / exact-match on eval set).
5) Profiling artifacts — perf counters, NVTX, and kernel timing breakdown exported as JSON.

Marta: Example harness invocation (rough):
```
# calibration (if model requires):
python tools/calibrate.py --model ./mymodel --dataset eval_prompts.json --quant int8 --out calib_int8.json

# warmup (populate KV + kernels)
python tools/run_bench.py --model ./mymodel --quant int8 --calib calib_int8.json --warmup_tokens 2048 --warmup_iters 20 --batch_profile batch_profile.json --seed 42 --power_cap 250

# steady-state (measure)
python tools/run_bench.py --model ./mymodel --quant int8 --calib calib_int8.json --measure_iters 200 --batch_profile batch_profile.json --out results_int8.json
```

Carlos: A few gotchas from profiling:
- If calibration shifts ranges enough, some ops take different kernel paths (e.g. fallback to fp32 kernels or slower dtype-conversion kernels). That kills latency. We should log kernel choices.
- KV cache behavior: we saw warmup size matters. If you include very short prompts only in warmup, KV lifetime differs and prefix caching hit rate drops on long prompts. Capture "kv_hit_rate" in the harness.
- Batching heuristics: dynamic micro-batching increases throughput but can spike p95. Record batch size distribution during the run.

Dina: On tokenization parity: make sure every run uses the same tokenizer binary, same pre/post-processing. Even whitespace differences change BPE alignment and token counts -> unfair perf/quality numbers. Use canonicalize_prompts.py to normalize. Also record tokens_per_prompt.

Ben: For comparing FP8 vs INT8 vs 4-bit: do we require the same calibration dataset and same number of calibration steps? Otherwise quality is incomparable.

Marta: Yes. Mandate a shared calibration set (we already have eval_prompts.json) and a fixed calibration config (random seed, blocking size). Also record calibration statistics: per-tensor scale histograms, saturation rates. Add fields to output JSON: "calib_seed", "saturation_pct", "scale_histogram_ref".

PerfBot: [automated] Reminder: attach NVProf/Nsys tarball and kernel_choice.json for traceability. Add label `quant-protocol-v1` to thread.

Carlos: We should also capture scheduler effects: if kernel selection chooses a slower but lower-memory kernel under a tighter memory pressure scenario (e.g., with larger batch or kv lifetime), that hides as regression. Suggest toggles: force-kernel alias to validate. Example: `--force_kernel gemm_int8_fast` and `--force_kernel gemm_fp32_stable`.

Marta: Good point. Include a `kernel_lock` field in run metadata. When running fair comparisons, do two modes: 1) best-kernel-per-variant (what users will see), 2) locked-kernel-equality (force same algorithm family across variants). Compare both.

Dina: For result keys, let's standardize: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, gpu_mem_peak_mb, kv_hit_rate, calib_saturation_pct, quality_perplexity, kernel_choices (list), batch_dist (histogram). Keep those names exact.

Ben: How long should warmup be? We saw diminishing returns after ~10k tokens for some LLMs. Maybe default warmup_tokens=4096 and warmup_iters=50, but allow per-model tuning documented in model_profiles.json.

Marta: Agreed. And log "warmup_done" boolean; if warmup didn't converge (kv_hit_rate still rising) mark run as 'warmup_unstable' and abort comparison.

Carlos: Small note: FP8 runs often show lower mem but sometimes slower than INT8 due to extra fp8->fp16 convert ops. Add a per-op overhead counter in kernel timing breakdown to catch that.

Marta: I'll push a PR with a minimal harness change to output the JSON keys Dina listed and a README describing the protocol. Plan: run a small sweep (fp8/int8/4bit) on the 2 test models next week and post results. Anyone object?

Ben: No objections, sounds solid. :+1:

Dina: Thanks — will prepare canonical prompts and tokenization checks.

PerfBot: [automated] Label `quant-protocol-v1` applied. Run template: `quant_run_v1.yaml` created in /tmp for the team.

Marta: Great. I'll open the PR and link the first sweep once runs finish.
